explanation:
The retina is the innermost layer of the eye and contains the specialized photoreceptor cells (rods and cones) that detect light and convert it into electrical signals for the brain. In contrast, the cornea is the transparent outer covering that focuses light, the sclerotic layer (sclera) is the tough white outer protective layer, and the conjunctiva is the thin membrane covering the front of the eye and inner eyelids.
